title: Senior's toolkit: nano and your editor setup
summary: The nano keys and editor settings experienced people rely on, and how to choose which editor git, crontab and sudo open.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: nano and your editor setup
steps.body: On a server you edit one config file fast and leave. On your laptop you decide which editor every tool opens. These keys and settings cover both.

toolkit.what: Open a file with line numbers, straight at the line an error message named.
flags: start on line 42 (`+42,10` also sets the column)
keep a backup copy as `file~` when saving

toolkit.what: Write out (save) and exit. Ctrl+X on a changed file asks `Save modified buffer?`: answer Y, then Enter to keep the name.
flags: exit, asking to save if needed

toolkit.what: Search, search and replace, and go to a line number. The three keys you need to fix a setting in a long file.
flags: replace: asks for the text, the replacement, then Y/N/A per match

toolkit.what: Undo, redo, cut the current line, paste. Ctrl+K several times cuts a block of lines that Ctrl+U pastes back in one go.
flags: copy the line without cutting it

toolkit.what: Edit a root-owned file with your own editor and settings. sudo copies the file, you edit the copy, sudo writes it back. Safer than running the whole editor as root.
flags: the editor it opens, checked in that order

toolkit.what: Sets the editor that `crontab -e`, `git commit`, `kubectl edit` and many others open. Put it in `~/.bashrc` once.
flags: Debian/Ubuntu helper that picks one for `crontab -e`

toolkit.what: Makes git open VS Code for messages and `rebase -i`. `--wait` makes the command block until you close the tab; without it git sees an empty message and aborts.
flags: return only when the file is closed
wins over VISUAL and EDITOR for git

steps.prompt: Match each nano key to what it does.
`sudo nginx -t` says `unknown directive "proxy_passs" in /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/api:31`. What is the quickest way to get there?
options: `sudo nano /etc/nginx/sites-enabled/api`, then scroll down counting lines
steps.explain: `+31` opens on the line the error names and `-l` shows the numbers so you can be sure. (`sudoedit` with nano works just as well.) Then run `nginx -t` again before you reload.

steps.prompt: You set `git config --global core.editor code`. Now every `git commit` ends at once with `Aborting commit due to empty commit message.` while VS Code opens the file. Why?
options: Without `--wait` the `code` command returns at once, so git reads the still-empty file
VS Code cannot edit files in `.git/`
The commit has no staged changes
steps.explain: git waits for the editor process to exit, then reads the message. `code` hands the file to the running window and exits. `code --wait` blocks until you close the tab.

steps.prompt: Edit `/etc/hosts` as root safely, with nano as the editor.
steps.explain: `sudoedit` runs your editor as you on a temporary copy and writes it back as root. `SUDO_EDITOR` picks the editor for that one command.

steps.prompt: Which setting decides the editor each of these opens?

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Set `VISUAL`, `EDITOR` and git's `core.editor` on day one on every machine you use, so nothing drops you into an editor you did not pick. On servers, open configs with `nano -l +LINE` or `sudoedit`, and always run the service's config test (`nginx -t`, `sshd -t`) before you reload.
